title: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts) with BBFC classification
title_ar: الجزء الثاني من «نايفز آوت»: البصلة الزجاجية

BBFC: 12A for cinema (24 Nov 2022) citing infrequent strong language, moderate sex references, violence, drug misuse; 12 for streaming/video.

athar_applications: Reference for the 'replay the same scene with the missing information' reveal, which ATHAR can implement as a post-case evidence timeline replay.
Shows that the same title is rated two bands higher in the Saudi storefront than in the US: ATHAR should design to the strictest Gulf rating, not to US/UK ratings.
limitations: Platform labels are not the national regulator's classification; GCAM/Saudi cinema rating was not checked.
Analysed from official metadata only; the film itself was not viewed for this record.

title: Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts) with BBFC classification
title_ar: «استيقظ أيها الميت»: لغز من سلسلة نايفز آوت

Third Benoit Blanc film; festival premiere Sep 2025 per Wikidata (Q115931717), runtime about 144 min.
athar_applications: Confirms the franchise as the current mainstream 'whodunit' expectation-setter for 16+ audiences in the Gulf.
Long-form (2.5 h) single-sitting format contrasts with ATHAR's 20–40 min sessions: borrow the reveal craft, not the length.
limitations: Not viewed; content analysis limited to official descriptors.
Netflix SA label may reflect Netflix's own mapping rather than a Saudi regulator decision.

title: Sherlock (BBC One, 2010–2017) — BBC programme page
key_findings: BBC programme page lists 13 episodes in total across 4 series; Wikidata gives 90-min episodes, 25 Jul 2010 to 15 Jan 2017.
Netflix SA labels it 18+; Netflix US labels it TV-14 (fetched 2026-10-27).
BBFC rated the special 'The Abominable Bride' 15 (strong violence, drug references, suicide).
athar_applications: Its on-screen text overlays for observations ('mind palace', floating deductions) shaped teen expectations of how deduction 'looks'; ATHAR's evidence board can show inference chains visually but must expose uncertainty, unlike the infallible TV Holmes.
Trademark caution: 'Sherlock' marks are registered (see ATH-SRC-1833); use generic language in marketing.
limitations: Saudi Netflix 18+ label means it cannot be recommended as viewing for ATHAR's 13–17 users in KSA.
Series not re-watched for this record.

title: Only Murders in the Building (Hulu Original, 2021– ) — Hulu series page
key_findings: Hulu lists 5 seasons (50 episodes), premiere 31 Aug 2021, rated TV-MA; episode 1 runs about 33 min.
Premise: three neighbours bond over a true-crime podcast, then investigate a death in their building and record their own podcast.
Romper (2022) notes TV-MA but reports a Common Sense Media 14+ recommendation; ratings sources disagree.
athar_applications: Model for 'investigators who publish their reasoning': ATHAR can let teams record a short case summary (audio or text) as the final deliverable, assessed with the reasoning rubric.
Shows amateur sleuthing framed as comedy and friendship lowers the darkness of murder themes, a tone option for 16–18 content.
limitations: TV-MA in the US; availability and rating in Arab storefronts (Disney+/OSN+) not verified.
Self-mocking satire of true-crime fandom may not transfer to Arab audiences.

title: Wednesday (Netflix, 2022– ) — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts)

Netflix tags include 'Amateur Detective', 'Teen TV Shows', 'TV Mysteries'; Wikidata lists 16 episodes (Q105553568).
Teen protagonist investigates mysteries at a boarding school (official synopsis).
athar_applications: Strong evidence that the teen-detective-at-school frame is mainstream; ATHAR's school-based cases fit an established taste.
The 18+ Saudi label shows that gothic horror and violence push teen-frame stories out of the teen band in KSA: ATHAR must keep the frame but not the gore.
limitations: Popularity in Arab markets not measured here (no regional viewing data).
Not re-watched for this record.

title: Enola Holmes (2020) — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts) with BBFC classification

Its fourth-wall asides to camera are a model for an in-case narrator who asks the player to predict before revealing.

Rating labels are platform-level.

title: Enola Holmes 2 (2022) — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts) with BBFC classification

First professional case: a missing-girl investigation (official synopsis); about 129 min (Wikidata).
athar_applications: Concrete example that a franchise can jump from teen to adult band in the Saudi storefront between instalments; ATHAR needs per-case rating review, not per-series.
Supports a content checklist on bloody images and injury detail (BBFC descriptors) as triggers for the 16–18 band.
limitations: Reason for the SA 18+ label is not published on the page; inference only.

title: Agatha Christie's Poirot (ITV, 1989–2013) — official Agatha Christie film & TV page
key_findings: Debuted on ITV in 1989, ran almost 25 years: 13 series and 70 episodes, starring David Suchet (official page).
Rights holder claims broadcast in 200 countries (self-reported).
Wikidata (Q391101): 8 Jan 1989 to 13 Nov 2013.
athar_applications: Canonical 'gathering of suspects' reveal format; ATHAR's final accusation screen can borrow the structure (each suspect cleared with one stated reason).
Trademarks POIROT and AGATHA CHRISTIE are registered (ATH-SRC-1832): no name use in ATHAR marketing.
limitations: Official page is promotional; no age rating given there.
Age ratings for the series vary by episode and were not collected.

title: Kenneth Branagh's Poirot film trilogy (2017, 2022, 2023) — BBFC classification records
key_findings: Murder on the Orient Express (2017): 12A for moderate violence and occasional bloody images.
Death on the Nile (2022): 12A for moderate violence, bloody images, injury detail and sex references.
A Haunting in Venice (2023): 12A for moderate threat, violence and suicide references (BBFC release page a-haunting-in-venice).

The novels are cataloged separately as ATH-SRC-0116 and ATH-SRC-0118; films are distinct copyrighted works: link-only.
limitations: UK classification only; Gulf ratings not collected.
Descriptors summarise; they do not grade intensity for 13–15 specifically.

Rating reflects the series as a whole; per-episode intensity not reviewed.

title: Detective Conan (anime) — Netflix title page with BBFC classification of the 2026 film
key_findings: Netflix SA title page shows 16+ but states the title is currently not available to watch in Saudi Arabia; Netflix US: TV-14, about 24-min episodes in 3 collections, audio English/Japanese only (re-checked 2026-10-27). [Corrected/Clarified 2026-10-27 by deep-card review]
TV anime began 8 Jan 1996 on Nippon TV; episodes about 25 min (Wikidata Q5363072). Manga cataloged as ATH-SRC-0138.

BBFC: 'Detective Conan: Fallen Angel of the Highway' 12A (cinema 12 Jun 2026; moderate violence, threat, injury detail). The 12A was reached after cuts made at the distributor's request (blood spurts in one scene); an uncut 15 was available. [Corrected/Clarified 2026-10-27 by deep-card review]
athar_applications: The 25-min case-of-the-week with a single explanation scene is the format most Arab 13–20s grew up with via Arabic dubbing (see ATH-SRC-2011, ATH-SRC-2012): a strong anchor for ATHAR session length.
Shows that the same IP is labelled 16+ on Netflix SA while dubbed broadcasts were children's TV: content edit level matters more than the IP.
limitations: Netflix carries a limited subset; Arabic dub not offered on the Netflix listing.
Murder-heavy plots; ATHAR must not copy case content (copyright and teen safety).

title: Spacetoon Go: Anime & Cartoon — App Store listing (SA)
key_findings: Listing (released 24 May 2019, updated 22 Oct 2026, rated 4+) claims 10,000+ Arabic-dubbed episodes and movies and names Detective Conan first in its anime list.

Its family-safety pitch (kids mode, profiles, ad-free premium) is the bar ATHAR's parent-facing messaging must meet.
limitations: Catalogue and dub-dialect details not verified inside the app.
Rating count is a weak usage proxy.

title: بعد نجاحه عالميًا.. «المحقق كونان الجديد» في صالات السينما العربية 27 مايو (Al Bayan)

Places the Arabic Conan audience in Gulf cinemas, i.e., teen-to-adult nostalgia demand (useful for 18–24 segment messaging).

Does not give the year Conan first aired on Spacetoon (gap G22 remains).

Its to-camera case recap is a model for an end-of-case reflection prompt.

Arab-market viewing not measured.

title: Carmen Sandiego: To Steal or Not to Steal (Netflix interactive special, 2020) — Netflix title page
title_ar: كارمن سانديغو: أتسرق أم لا (حلقة تفاعلية)
key_findings: Netflix SA: 7+; US: TV-Y7; synopsis: 'You drive the action' to help Carmen rescue friends during a heist.
Listed by What's on Netflix among the interactive specials discontinued on 1 Dec 2024.
The Netflix title page still resolved on 2026-10-27 (playability not tested).

title: Netflix Removing All But Four Interactive Specials in December 2024 (What's on Netflix)
key_findings: Published 4 Nov 2024: Netflix confirmed it was discontinuing most interactive titles from 1 Dec 2024; a Netflix representative told The Verge 'The technology served its purpose, but is now limiting'.
Last interactive release was 'Choose Love' (Aug 2023); four titles remained, including Black Mirror: Bandersnatch.
About 19 titles listed for removal, most of them for children (e.g., Carmen Sandiego, Captain Underpants, Boss Baby).
athar_applications: Lesson: choose-your-path video alone did not sustain a format at the world's largest streamer; ATHAR's interactivity must add reasoning value (evidence handling, justification), not only branching.
Avoid building on any single platform's proprietary interactive player.
limitations: Trade blog, not Netflix itself; cites The Verge.
No engagement data explaining the decision.

title: Odd Squad (PBS Kids, 2014–2022) — Netflix title page with BBFC classification

Agency/office framing (agents with ranks) works without crime or victims.
limitations: Aimed at 5–9; tone too young for ATHAR core.
No learning-outcome data cited here.

limitations: Heist/revenge drama, not fair-play detection.

title: «MBC» توقف مسلسلاً يتناول قصة شاب من قبيلة عريقة بالخليج قبل عرضه بساعات.. مسلسل «رشاش» يثير غضباً وجدلاً (Arabic Post)
key_findings: 22 Jan 2021: Shahid (MBC Group) postponed 'Rashash' hours before its planned premiere, without stating a reason, after backlash.
The 8-part Saudi crime drama (60-min weekly episodes; written by Tony Jordan with others; directed by Colin Teague) fictionalised a real 1980s highway robber from the Otaibi tribe who was executed.

The tribe's official forum condemned it as inciting discord; critics argued portraying a real person required the heirs' consent. Wikidata (Q107394818) records the series' eventual start on 9 Jul 2021.
athar_applications: Hard rule for ATHAR: no cases based on identifiable real people, families or tribes in the Gulf; use fully fictional names checked against prominent family/tribe names.
Real-crime adaptation carries reputational risk even for the region's largest broadcaster.
limitations: Second-hand reporting; Shahid gave no official reason.
One case; does not quantify risk.

title: 'Room 207' Wins New Fans for Authors of Egyptian Horror Fiction (Al-Fanar Media)
title_ar: «الغرفة 207» تكسب جمهوراً جديداً لأدب الرعب المصري
key_findings: 10 Dec 2022: 'Room 207', based on Ahmed Khaled Tawfik's 2017 novel, topped Shahid's most-watched list (as reported).
Format: a hotel employee tries to solve the mystery of one room whose guests undergo profound changes; horror, mystery and fantasy elements.
Part of a wave of Egyptian screen adaptations of Tawfik's work after Paranormal (ATH-SRC-0737).
athar_applications: A single recurring location with a new 'guest' per episode is a cheap, anthology-friendly structure ATHAR can reuse (one lab/office, one new case visitor each week).
Confirms Tawfik-branded mystery-horror as the strongest Egyptian youth reference.
limitations: No viewing numbers; ranking claim not independently verified.
Episode count and length not stated.

title: «رهن التحقيق» دراما بوليسية سعودية بإشراف هوليوودي (Ajel)
title_ar: «رهن التحقيق» دراما بوليسية سعودية بإشراف هوليوودي
key_findings: 16 Sep 2020: Shahid VIP exclusive Saudi police drama starring Faisal Al-Dokhi and Reem Al-Habib; directed by Ali Al-Attas; written by Noura Abu Shousha and Sarah Al-Ghabra; script supervision by Hollywood writer-producer Jill Gold Smith (as reported).
Each episode presents a past crime narrated by young investigator Turki, who is himself under internal-affairs interrogation for allegedly illegal methods and must justify his reasoning.
The series combines live actors with cartoon counterparts of the characters.
athar_applications: The frame of an investigator justifying each past case to an auditor maps directly to ATHAR's reasoning-assessment: the player's case report is reviewed by an in-world auditor who asks 'why is this evidence enough?'
Saudi precedent for procedural ethics (legality of methods) as drama, supporting ATHAR's young-investigator-within-the-law frame (KO-CD-02-012).
limitations: Press preview only; reception and ratings unknown.
Spelling of the supervising writer's name as given in Arabic press.

title: موعد عرض «القصة الكاملة».. 5 جرائم مستوحاة من أحداث حقيقية (Akhbar El Yom)
title_ar: موعد عرض «القصة الكاملة».. 5 جرائم مستوحاة من أحداث حقيقية
key_findings: 4 Aug 2026: Shahid announced season 1 of 'Al-Qissa al-Kamila' from 28 Aug 2026: 5 standalone stories, 3 episodes each, each with its own writers, directors and cast.
Inspired by cases from director Sameh Sanad's YouTube programme of the same name (contract reported in ATH-SRC-0766).
Stories draw on notorious Egyptian crimes, including the 'Tourbini' child-murder case and the Beni Mazar massacre.
athar_applications: Validates the 3-episode case arc as a current Arab streaming format: ATHAR seasons can be built of 3-part cases (setup / investigation / resolution).
Counter-example on content: dramatising real child victims is precisely what ATHAR excludes.
limitations: Pre-release announcement; reception and rating not verified.
No age rating stated in the article.

title: OSN to launch new Original 'Kayd Majhool' this March (BroadcastPro ME)
key_findings: 14 Feb 2021: OSN announced 'Kayd Majhool (Anonymous)', an eight-episode psychological thriller debuting 18 Mar 2021 on OSN Ya Hala Al Oula and the OSN app.
Two parallel stories (an investigator on two murders; a struggling tailor-taxi driver) converge at season end.
Offered with English subtitles and English dubbing for wider regional audiences; directed by Alsadeer Masoud, written by Mohamed Abu Laban and Lewa'a Yazajy.
athar_applications: Dual-perspective structure (investigator vs. suspect's life) is a reusable pattern for ATHAR's 16–18 cases, letting players see motive context without graphic content.
Shows Arab originals invest in dubbing into English, not only subtitles: ATHAR's bilingual mode should consider voiced English for diaspora/international schools.
limitations: Trade press announcement; ratings and reception unknown.

title: في حصاد الدراما التليفزيونية.. «الجريمة» تسيطر على مسلسلات 2016 (Masrawy)
title_ar: في حصاد الدراما التليفزيونية.. «الجريمة» تسيطر على مسلسلات 2016
key_findings: 27 Dec 2016 review: crime and suspense dominated Egyptian TV drama in 2016, with series built around solving a crime committed at the start and revealed across the season.
Examples: Saqout Hor, Al-Mizan (courtroom), Fawq Mostawa al-Shubuhat, Ras al-Ghoul, Grand Hotel (a man searches a hotel for his missing sister and uncovers the owners' secrets), Shahadat Milad.
athar_applications: Mainstream Ramadan TV has trained Arab audiences in the 30-episode 'who did it' slow reveal: ATHAR can use season-long meta-mysteries across short cases.
Courtroom drama (Al-Mizan) is an accepted Arab genre, supporting a later 'courtroom/argument' mode.
limitations: Editorial roundup, no audience data.
Egypt only.

title: Netflix film Perfect Strangers challenges Middle East taboos (Al Jazeera)
title_ar: فيلم «أصحاب ولا أعز» يتحدى المحرمات في الشرق الأوسط
key_findings: 4 Feb 2022: Netflix's first Arabic-language film quickly became the most watched on the service in the region after release on 20 Jan 2022 (as reported).
Its themes (sexuality, homosexuality, infidelity) triggered a public debate, especially in Egypt.
Remake of an Italian film said to be the most remade in cinema history (article's claim).
athar_applications: Controversy in the region clusters around sexuality and family morality more than crime: ATHAR's content policy should treat romance/sexual content as a stricter line than non-graphic crime.
Shows high reach does not protect a title from backlash; parents and media figures act as gatekeepers.
limitations: Not a mystery title; included for regional controversy patterns.
Viewing rank claim not independently verified.

title: أغرب القضايا (Aghrab Al-Qadaya, Egyptian radio crime drama, 1968) — elCinema work page
key_findings: Egyptian radio series (1968), episodes of about 22 minutes, genre mystery.
Police radio drama on the strangest crimes worldwide, building to decoding the crime and identifying the culprit however clever (database synopsis).
Cast includes Mahmoud Azmy, Amina Rizk, Samiha Ayoub; directed by Abdou Diab and Tarek Diab.
athar_applications: Arabic precedent for the 20–25 min audio whodunit with a closing reveal: ATHAR's audio pilot sits in a 60-year national tradition, useful for parent/teacher legitimacy.
Candidate for licensed nostalgia content or a 'from the radio archive' lesson only via Maspero (rights not established).
limitations: Database page, not the broadcaster's archive; episode count unknown.
Rights belong to Egyptian national radio (NMA); no reuse permission.

title: طاهر أبو فاشا — profile page (Maspero / National Media Authority)
title_ar: طاهر أبو فاشا (صاحب الحلقات الإذاعية «ألف ليلة وليلة»)
topics: One Thousand and One Nights radio serial
key_findings: Official NMA profile: Taher Abu Fasha (1912–1989) wrote more than 200 radio works.
His radio 'Alf Layla wa Layla' ran to more than 800 episodes broadcast over 26 years.
Also wrote radio serials for Kuwait Radio ('Alf Yawm wa Yawm').
athar_applications: Evidence of a deep Arab habit of nightly, short, serialized audio storytelling framed by a narrator (Shahrazad): ATHAR's narrator-led audio episodes have strong cultural fit.
The Three Apples tale (ATH-SRC-0139) inside the Nights is a PD detective story that ATHAR can adapt.
limitations: Profile page; no episode length or air dates per episode.
Radio recordings are NMA property; not reusable without licence.

title: Dollar (Netflix Lebanese series, 2019) — Netflix title page (SA and US storefronts)

title: جناية (Genaya) — Mics podcast, Apple Podcasts listing and RSS feed
key_findings: Ranked #2 in the Apple Podcasts overall chart in KSA and #10 in Kuwait (chart dated 2026-10-26, ATH-SRC-1551).

122 episodes from 5 Sep 2022 to 26 Oct 2026; median episode about 55 min (10th–90th percentile 27–83 min); hosts Mohammed Al-Baiz and Mohammed Al-Shaibani (earlier cataloged as a true-crime show in ATH-SRC-0763).

Since Oct 2026 the feed includes 'لعبة جناية' episodes: guests compete at the table to identify criminal, victim, weapon and scene card by card, mixing deduction with banter; regular episodes narrate investigation stories with sponsors; the feed describes the show as tracing and analysing 'real stories' (degree of fictionalisation unknown). Mics also sells a physical 'جناية' card game (SAR 115, 3-6 players, age 12+) linked from the episodes. [Corrected/Clarified 2026-10-27 by deep-card review]
athar_applications: Strongest evidence that a mainstream Gulf audience will listen to (and watch) people *playing* a deduction game: ATHAR can pilot a 'listen-and-play along' episode with pause points and a group-play mode for majlis/family.
Partner or benchmark for audio-first demand tests (KO-PO-08B-001).
limitations: Chart rank is a snapshot; audience is mostly adult; listener age unknown.
Feed self-category 'Society & Culture' differs from Apple genre 'Personal Journals'.
Episode count, median duration and date range computed by ATHAR from the show's public RSS feed (feed URL listed by the iTunes Lookup API), 2026-10-27.

title: قصص رون (Qisas Ron) — Apple Podcasts listing and RSS feed
key_findings: Top-100 in all six Arab storefronts in the snapshot (KSA #7, Morocco #11, Kuwait #12, Jordan #17, Egypt #30, UAE #50; ATH-SRC-1551).
914 episodes since 17 Nov 2023; median about 11 min (10th–90th percentile 6.5–31 min); near-daily posting of personal and social stories in Gulf dialect, with compilation episodes.
Apple genre 'Drama/Fiction'; feed carries discount-code advertising.
athar_applications: Short (10–15 min), daily, conversational dialect storytelling can reach the top of Arab charts: supports an ATHAR daily micro-case or 'case of the day' in audio.
Shows the habit-forming power of frequency over production value.
